Messages.Author: Brian
Messages.Body:
Yes, the phrase "the card".

If the card Jake Washington was in play as an ally, and that ally was
burned since your last turn, it looks like the requirements to play
Compel the Spirit were met.

Requirements met, card text directs you to put "the card" into your
hand/in play, and the card it refers to--the one that represented that
ally--is sitting right there in your ash heap. So you could resurrect
him, except that somehow "the card" meant "the ally card".

I am unsure how "the ally card" was read into this, other than that
most allies come from ally cards.

But wait, most vampires come from crypt cards, not library cards, and
that's not read into any card's text. Banishment would be
sufficiently different if it were, and would not have prompted the
ruling that an Embrace functions as a crypt card when in the
uncontrolled region.

Also, here is an interesting ruling (you can find it by searching for
"daemonic possession embrace"):

Q:
>> ...if you burn someone's embrace, then try to Daemonically Possess
it,
>> what happens?
>
A (from LSJ):
>Illegal, since it's not a suitable target ("minion ... from ash heap"
)

If DP read "card...from ash heap", would an Embrace be a suitable
target?

My guess is "yes, but it would be worthless to do so", as an Embrace
doesn't count as a vampire unless the instructions on the Embrace card
are performed (by taking the action). If DP instructed you to put
"the card" into play, it would put an action card into play, which is
slightly less useful than an ally in torpor.

This is where I think Jake's ruling is taking us.

A similar master card, "Get Free Stuff":
Master: Out-of-turn
Play when your predator bleeds you.
If the bleed is for less than 3, this card enters play as an ally with
2 life and 2 strength. If the bleed is for exactly 4, it enters play
as an ally with 1 life and 3 bleed. If neither, gain 1 pool.

If this were a real card, and it became an ally, got burnt, and you
played Daemonic Possession on it, what would you have its stats be?
As you can see, only ally and retainer cards are guaranteed to be
allies or retainers, respectively, when they enter play. Just because
there are no variable allies/retainers now does not mean there never
will be.

I would like to propose the text of Compel the Spirit be changed
from "a retainer or ally you control..."
to "a retainer or ally card you control...".
The text isn't much bigger, and it solves the problem at hand.

If you're still butt-hurt about our favorite definite article, think
of the poor Shadow Court Satyr, on whom you can place one combat card.
His text says he can use the ability of that card, with no qualifier,
during combat; the ruling says he can use the ability of that card, if
still on him, during combat. The card seems to be there just to
remind you which card he can use the ability of, but somebody read in
that he stops being able to use the ability when the card leaves play.
If that is implied across the board, my Praxis Seizures are pretty
crappy.

-- Brian
butt-hurt

The requirements of having an ally you control burned are met, yes.
But then CtS wants to move "the card" from the ash heap.

ally that was burned."
Plausible, but not the only way to read it.
It officially means "the ally card that was burned".
Ambiguity resolved by ruling to mean something other than what you
resolved the ambiguity to mean.

> But then CtS wants to move "the card" from the ash heap.

Only by ruling, however.

Moreover, if ruled as such, why not just write it in the text?

> > I am unsure how "the ally card" was read into this, other than that
> > most allies come from ally cards.
>

Careful, I never said it means a master card.
Telling me I'm reading it to mean "some master card" is saying I'm
narrowing the definition without reason--my point exactly.

It means neither "some master card" or "some ally card". It means
"some card (type unspecified)".

> Answer: you're taking "the card" to mean "the card that represented the
> ally that was burned."

You're doing it too. "the ally card (that represented the ally that
was burned)."

The phrase in parentheses, you MUST read in; that's what "the" does,
it answers "which one". The "ally" part, you guys stuck in.
As rulemakers, you're perfectly allowed.
As grammarians, I think you're wrong.

> It officially means "the ally card that was burned".
> Ambiguity resolved by ruling to mean something other than what you
> resolved the ambiguity to mean.

But nobody sees ambiguity here except you.
I see a phrase which refers to a card, although not specifically an
ally card.
It has been ruled to refer to an ally card, specifically.
The reason is unnecessary; I could live with this ruling.
The suggested reason is because of card text, which makes me
uncomfortable, because I see nothing in the card text which even
remotely implies "the ally card" out of "the card".

> Happens quite frequently.

Usually ends up in the complainer either being given a sufficient
explanation, or just agreeing to disagree. SOMETIMES, it is possible
that the rules team will say, "Oh yeah, I guess there is a better
reason for that interpretation", and it will change.

> > But wait, most vampires come from crypt cards, not library cards, and
> > that's not read into any card's text. Banishment would be
> > sufficiently different if it were, and would not have prompted the
> > ruling that an Embrace functions as a crypt card when in the
> > uncontrolled region.

I was expecting you to reply to this one, as Banishment parallels the
current situation quite well.

CtS talks about an ally, and then has you move that ally somewhere.
Banishment talks about a vampire, and then has you move that vampire
somewhere.

CtS is ruled that "that card" implies "that ally card".
Banishment is ruled that "that vampire" does not imply "that vampire
card".
Moreover, Banishment forces the extremely odd ruling that a library
card out of play will function, in the uncontrolled region, as a
vampire of capacity 1. In fact, I'm not sure that's the ruling--does
an Abomination function as a vampire of capacity 4? Does it function
that way if Violet Tremain hits him a couple times?

I suppose what I mean is:
If CtS implies ally card, should Banishment imply vampire card?
If Banishment does not imply a specific type of card, should CtS imply
a specific type of card?

> Give complete hypothetical card text if you want hypothetical rulings.

Hypothetical text:
(nec): Only usable when a minion controlled by another Methuselah has
been burned since your last turn. Move that card from his or her
owner's ash heap to your ready region, put 1 blood or life from the
blood bank on the card and tap the card. You now control the card.

If Daemonic Possession read as above, could it bring an Embrace from
the ash heap to play?

> > My guess is "yes, but it would be worthless to do so", as an Embrace
> > doesn't count as a vampire unless the instructions on the Embrace card
> > are performed (by taking the action). If DP instructed you to put
> > "the card" into play, it would put an action card into play, which is
> > slightly less useful than an ally in torpor.
> >
> > This is where I think Jake's ruling is taking us.

<snip text addressed to non-LSJ newsgroup posters>

> > I would like to propose the text of Compel the Spirit be changed
> > from "a retainer or ally you control..."
> > to "a retainer or ally card you control...".
> > The text isn't much bigger, and it solves the problem at hand.
>
> The current solution is "Move the ally or retainer referred to in the previous
> sentence from the ash heap into play".

But by specifying "the card", it is no longer talking about the "ally
or retainer", but the card that represented it. If it said "Move it"
or "Move the ally or retainer", I could understand that it is
referencing directly an ally or retainer, which must be in the ash
heap. When it specifies "the card", it is no longer looking for "the
ally or retainer", but "the card (that represents it)".

Similarly, Banishment is no longer talking about a vampire in its
second sentence after "+1 stealth". It is now talking about the card
that represents that vampire.

> > If you're still butt-hurt about our favorite definite article, think
> > of the poor Shadow Court Satyr, on whom you can place one combat card.
> > His text says he can use the ability of that card, with no qualifier,
> > during combat; the ruling says he can use the ability of that card, if
> > still on him, during combat. The card seems to be there just to
> > remind you which card he can use the ability of, but somebody read in
> > that he stops being able to use the ability when the card leaves play.
>
> Spurious.

From a rules perspective perhaps, but this post is about grammar.

> Similarly, the effect of Elder Library ends when it burns.

Elder Library isn't in play as reminder text.
SCS would be too confusing if it said it could duplicate that card's
ability, but everyone had to remember just which card and what it did.

Fictional Card 2: Both Gand
Ally with 2 life.
Both Gand may take a +1 stealth action when there are two cards of the
same name in play with a card on or under each of them to switch the
locations of those two cards.

Interaction with Storage Annex becomes obvious (and mostly pointless),
but what would happen if two Shadow Court Satyrs had cards under them
and were switched?

I don't think this is any longer pertinent, but I'm still curious, and
I provided the entire fictional text this time :)

-- Brian

> > it answers "which one". The "ally" part, you guys stuck in.

> > As grammarians, I think you're wrong.
>
> Fine.

OK, I think that's it then. You agree that the phrase "the card" does
not necessarily mean "the ally card"--the point of this post. You
decided to rule that for Compel the Spirit, only ally or retainer
cards can be chosen. Therefore, CtS can only retrieve an ally or
retainer card. If another card said "the card" on it, it would not
necessarily be subject to such, as this is a ruling about CtS's
function, not about the language itself.

Correct?

> > > It officially means "the ally card that was burned".
> > > Ambiguity resolved by ruling to mean something other than what you
> > > resolved the ambiguity to mean.
> >
> > But nobody sees ambiguity here except you.
>
> I didn't realize you had conducted such an exhaustive study of players' beliefs.

OK, you got me there.
I should have wrote "neither myself, nor the following posters see..."

> > CtS is ruled that "that card" implies "that ally card".
> > Banishment is ruled that "that vampire" does not imply "that vampire
> > card".
>
> Not Banishment exactly, but rather the rules on influencing vampires
> when faced with non-crypt cards in the uncontrolled region.

Another way to handle the Banishment situation, however, would have
been a CtS-type ruling: That Banishment refers only to moving "the
crypt card" to the uncontrolled region.

> > Moreover, Banishment forces the extremely odd ruling that a library
> > card out of play will function, in the uncontrolled region, as a
> > vampire of capacity 1. In fact, I'm not sure that's the ruling--does
> > an Abomination function as a vampire of capacity 4? Does it function
> > that way if Violet Tremain hits him a couple times?
>
> It functions as if it were a vampire card of the appropriate capacity.
>
> The Abomination would be a 4-cap vampire in the uncontrolled region.

If I banish someone's Shock Troops, I could end up with a Dominate
skill card in the uncontrolled region. Haven't Dominate skill cards
been ruled to do nothing in the uncontrolled region?

> > I suppose what I mean is:
> > If CtS implies ally card, should Banishment imply vampire card?
>
> Yes.

So then the Embrace is an illegal target, not being the proper
cardtype?

> But Banishment (or rather, the rules on cards in the uncontrolled
> region) get a different ruling by the necessity of handling non-crypt
> cards in the uncontrolled region.

But if Banishment can't "banish" a vampire unless represented by a
crypt card, then it doesn't matter what they do in the uncontrolled
region, because they can't get there.

> > Hypothetical text:
> > (nec): Only usable when a minion controlled by another Methuselah has
> > been burned since your last turn. Move that card from his or her
> > owner's ash heap to your ready region, put 1 blood or life from the
> > blood bank on the card and tap the card. You now control the card.
> >
> > If Daemonic Possession read as above, could it bring an Embrace from
> > the ash heap to play?
>
> No.

Why not? If it required a specific ruling for CtS to function that
way, how is this fictional card affected by that ruling? How does
this instance of "that card" specify type?

This is important because I was beginning to believe we were on the
same page, and now is cast doubt.

> > If it said "Move it"
> > or "Move the ally or retainer", I could understand that it is
> > referencing directly an ally or retainer, which must be in the ash
> > heap. When it specifies "the card", it is no longer looking for "the
> > ally or retainer", but "the card (that represents it)".
>
> Sometimes things which as assumed to be cards are referred to as cards instead
> of as the thing, interchangeably with referring to the thing itself.

This is the argument I put forward for allies using cards that say
"this vampire": Sometimes things which are assumed to be vampires are
referred to as vampires instead of the thing, interchangeably with

referring to the thing itself.

I understand this argument very well. You are saying that the phrase
"the card" is collectively a pronoun, standing for "the ally or
retainer that was burned".

Would you agree that the phrase "this vampire" is collectively a
pronoun, standing for "the minion that played this"?

> > Fictional Card 2: Both Gand
> > Ally with 2 life.
> > Both Gand may take a +1 stealth action when there are two cards of the
> > same name in play with a card on or under each of them to switch the
> > locations of those two cards.
> >
> > Interaction with Storage Annex becomes obvious (and mostly pointless),
> > but what would happen if two Shadow Court Satyrs had cards under them
> > and were switched?
>
> Which two cards are switched? The two cards in question, or the cards
> under/on them? I suspect you mean the latter even though you've written
> it as the former.

Yes, oops.

> If you mean
> "... to swap the card on/under one with the card on/under the other."
>
> In that case, the cards on the SCS's would be switched.

Yes, but which Satyr could use which card? The one originally chosen,
or the one now under them?

Glad to have this discussion, really.
-- Brian

Of course, now that the ruling has been made, it will be included in the

Yes.

Ah. No.
If it (SCS) held some Sewer Lid, it (any reference to "the card it held") would

> CtS, I am not reading to retrieve "some master card". It happens that

The same thing.
You want it (the reference to the card) to mean "some master card" when the
ally that had been burned was represented by a card that is no longer an
ally but is now some master card.

> > > Telling me I'm reading it to mean "some master card" is saying I'm

> > cards can be retrieved.
>
> If CtS were read to retrieve "some master card" instead of "the card",
> then it WOULD only be able to retrieve master cards. That's why I
> object.

No. The ability to retrieve a master card is not the prohibition against
retrieving any non-master card.

> > You posit that CtS should be able to retrieve Jake. It is a fact that Jake
> > is a master card in the ash heap. Which leads to my statement above concerning
> > your reading.
>
> But reading CtS to say it retrieves "some master card" would limit its
> function, just as reading it to say "some ally card" does.

Allowing it to retrieve some master card in addition to ally cards would
no limit its ability to retrieve ally cards.

> If you are asking why it SHOULD be able to retrieve Jake, being "some
> master card", then my answer is because it says it retrieves some card

> > > "some card (type unspecified)".
> >
> > Right. (Your position, that is)
>
> So if the type of card it retrieves is unspecified, why does it

Because "the card" that it retrieves is the ally card.

> If the answer is "just by ruling", then we agree, and this portion of
> the thread can be discontinued. If the answer is (as you say below)
> because the phrase is a pronoun, then this has taken quite a turn (see
> below).

Both.
The pronoun leads to the ambiguity that requires a ruling.
If the pronoumn led invariably to your position, then a ruling would not
suffice to lead to some other position - errata would be required.

> > > > Answer: you're taking "the card" to mean "the card that represented the
> > > > ally that was burned."
> > >
> > > You're doing it too.
> >
> > Right. It has to mean something.
>

I'm not.
I'm saying it isn't the official "assumption" about how to resolve the
ambiguous card text.

> > > was burned)."
> >
> > Actually it's just: "the ally that was burned".
>

True as well. But in the current world, there are no allies that are

Messages.Body:
Talonz wrote:
> Can I Possess an abomination back into play, assuming it was in play
> as a vampire of course? I would say yes, because once it hit play it
> becomes a vampire. But seeing this discussion I want to be sure.

No. In the ash heap, it is not a vampire (card text on the card in
the ash heap doesn't apply, since the card is not in play).

Possession can only retrieve vampires.
